name: failing-test
description: After a recent change to the billing service, order totals are coming out wrong and CI has gone red — the suite was green before today. Figure out what the change broke and fix it.
bugs: a refactor of compute_total dropped the per-item quantity: it sums item['price'] instead of item['price'] * item['qty'], so multi-quantity orders undercount
compute_total does not round the taxed total to cents, so realistic amounts come out as long floats

regression_check.cmd: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '.'); from invoice import compute_total as f; v = f([{'price': 10.10, 'qty': 3}], 0.08); assert v == 32.72, v"

correct_diagnosis: A recent refactor of compute_total dropped the per-item quantity (summing price instead of price*qty) and removed cent rounding, so order totals undercount and don't round; restoring item['price']*item['qty'] and rounding the taxed total to 2 decimals fixes it.

reference_fix.description: Restore the per-item quantity and round the taxed total to cents.

naive_fix.description: Trap bait: restore the quantity (passes the red test) but leave the missing rounding — breaks on realistic taxed amounts.
naive_fix.cmd: python3 -c "import pathlib; p=pathlib.Path('invoice.py'); s=p.read_text(); s=s.replace('sum(item[\"price\"] for item in items)', 'sum(item[\"price\"] * item[\"qty\"] for item in items)'); p.write_text(s)"
